claims.text: A CALPHAD-guided strategy can identify and optimize refractory HEA compositions.
CALPHAD can predict favorable multiphase equilibria that lead to high strength, ductility, and low density in RHEAs.
A disordered BCC matrix containing intermetallic precipitates is a favorable strengthening microstructure.
The intermetallic nanoprecipitates are coherent with the BCC matrix.
Coherent precipitates enhance dislocation pinning through local lattice distortions.
The baseline material is a single-phase or near-single-phase RHEA containing multiple principal refractory elements.
CALPHAD-based composition refinement can induce controlled precipitation of coherent intermetallic phases.
Managing atomic-size mismatch can produce targeted local lattice distortions.
Controlled heat treatment after casting promotes nanoprecipitate formation in the proposed RHEAs.
The structural mediator is a distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates within a disordered BCC matrix that generates severe local lattice distortions.
Multiple principal elements with differing atomic sizes cause atoms in HEAs to deviate from ideal lattice sites.
Local lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion.
The proposed strengthening mechanisms increase strength without sacrificing ductility.
Selecting low-density refractory elements reduces overall alloy weight.
The designed RHEAs will attain tensile strength approaching or exceeding 2 GPa.
The designed RHEAs will attain tensile ductility of at least 10%.
The designed RHEAs will have lower density than classical refractory alloys.
Traditional refractory alloys commonly exhibit a strength-ductility trade-off.
The hypothesis applies only where the chemistry and processing permit a disordered BCC matrix with coherent precipitates.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines sufficient ductility as at least 10%, whereas the falsification rule requires greater than 10%; a result of exactly 10% would simultaneously satisfy the prediction and fail the stated falsification criterion.
